Sentence (English): Have had this dishwasher just over a year now.
Comments (English): [ Cleans well, but ] || ---------------- || Have had this dishwasher just over a year now. Appliance is fairly quiet and does clean well,but. From the very beginning the fan would not turn off unless the door was opened or one just manually turned off the machine. We had a Whirlpool technician come to check it out, but of course could find nothing wrong after doing a diagnostic check. Then at exactly one year since install we noticed a water leak at the lower left side of the door. Now we have discovered that if we let the fan do it's drying for about three hours there is no leak ( ? ). We have noticed a vent at the lower left bottom of the door that does get wet and are wondering if that's where the water is dripping on the floor if the fan is not allowed to run at least the three hours. At any rate, it really is too much of a hassle to return the machine and then have to get another installed, so will just put up with it for now.

I decided on this after watching ads, watching live broadcasts, and comparing it to other products, but to be honest, it was a failed purchase. I didn't want to rush into a review, so I tried different cycles, using just the drying function, and adding the storage function. I also tried using dishes on the first layer and the second layer. First, the drying function is really poor. I used only the dish dryer before, but the basic 45-minute cycle dried them 100%. Even when I lifted the dishes and loaded them, there wasn't a single drop of moisture left. But with the Minix, it only dried for 1 hour and 25 minutes! And even after using the basic 1-hour drying cycle and 90-minute drying cycle, there was still moisture inside. Having to use the drying function again is a hassle. And while there is a storage function, its effectiveness is poor. After the basic drying cycle ends, the storage function doesn't activate immediately, but after 3 hours, so the dishes were still damp for 3 hours. Second, the washing performance is also disappointing. The number one reason I bought a dishwasher was because of the advertisements claiming it wouldn't leave water stains, but what do I do about the water stains that always remain on my dishes and cups? Was it overhyped, or is my product like this? I bought it because it's a non-perforated, usable product with a decent design, but with this level of performance at such a high price, I absolutely would not recommend it to anyone. And after washing the tumbler, there's a strange smell inside. I don't know if it's the detergent scent or something else. Oh! And if the rotating washing propeller gets caught on the dishes during the wash, it just stays in place and keeps running. There's no sensor, so if you don't check it regularly, it won't wash properly and will end. In conclusion, I don't recommend this dishwasher. The company needs to improve its features significantly.

Sentence (English): I bought a brand new dishwasher that hasn't been able to run for one cycle for a month now.
Comments (English): I bought a brand new dishwasher that hasn't been able to run for one cycle for a month now. The Home Depot installation technicians caused us so much grief and did not install this the day of the delivery. Then Home Depot refused to cover the faulty device since the technicians left the appliance at the house without installing it. Once installed by us, it didn't work due to a faulty control board, so we were forced to work through warranty to have a control board replaced. A cycle was started after the GE tech repair and was promising that it was fixed, but then a software update went through and now the dishwasher won't work again. GE technicians are coming out a second time to replace another part in hopes that this resolves the issue. I will say GE Technicians are wonderful to work with. However, Home Depot delivered the faulty device and won't stand behind it which is incredible disappointing. I recommend that you purchase appliances elsewhere, as no one should be in a situation where they are repairing a brand new appliance through warrant that has never been used.

Sentence (English): My kitchen is small and has no room for a built in dishwasher, so we've had to use portable ones for our house.
Comments (English): [ Worst Portable Dishwasher Ever ] || ---------------- || My kitchen is small and has no room for a built in dishwasher, so we've had to use portable ones for our house. The first two lasted seven years each. There were pros and cons to each, but both were bearable and worked well for a long time. This one, in constraint, is awful in every way with nothing to recommend it.The design is terrible. The controls are on the top of the door and are covered up when the door is shut. Not only does this cause numerous problems with things like even getting it to start (you have to hit the start button and then close the door not too fast nor too slow), but it's very easy to bump buttons and screw up settings when the dishwasher is open. To add insult to injury, the controls include a timer. What use this is when the controls are covered when in use is beyond me. If you peer through the crack, you can try to spot the numbers, but it's not very helpful as you're half guessing.The interior design is bad too. Every dishwasher is different, but I've never used another with such a bad layout on the racks. We can fit far fewer dishes into a load than we could with our previous dishwashers despite it being the same dimensions. The cycles take more than twice as long as well, which is lots of fun given how often we need to do two cycles a day now because of the poor layout.There are even more problems. The hose is set up very poorly and it won't go back into the body of the dishwasher unless it's still warm from having just finished the cycle. The seal on the inside of the door is placed so that the bottom rack runs over it. Because of this, the seal is now damaged and the dishwasher is leaking water. Multiple other things have broken on it as well and I've had it less than two years.Do not, for the love of all that's holy, buy this dishwasher. It is garbage. Note that the good reviews are generally from short times of ownership. I know there aren't a lot of options for portable dishwashers, but don't buy this one. It's a waste of money.

We can fit far fewer dishes into a load than we could with our previous dishwashers despite it being the same dimensions. The cycles take more than twice as long as well, which is lots of fun given how often we need to do two cycles a day now because of the poor layout.There are even more problems. The hose is set up very poorly and it won’t go back into the body of the dishwasher unless it’s still warm from having just finished the cycle. The seal on the inside of the door is placed so that the bottom rack runs over it. Because of this, the seal is now damaged and the dishwasher is leaking water. Multiple other things have broken on it as well and I’ve had it less than two years.Do not, for the love of all that’s holy, buy this dishwasher. It is garbage. Sentence (English): My kitchen is small and has no room for a built in dishwasher, so we've had to use portable ones for our house.
Comments (English): [ Worst Portable Dishwasher Ever ] || ---------------- || My kitchen is small and has no room for a built in dishwasher, so we've had to use portable ones for our house. The first two lasted seven years each. There were pros and cons to each, but both were bearable and worked well for a long time. This one, in constraint, is awful in every way with nothing to recommend it. The design is terrible. The controls are on the top of the door and are covered up when the door is shut. Not only does this cause numerous problems with things like even getting it to start (you have to hit the start button and then close the door not too fast nor too slow), but it's very easy to bump buttons and screw up settings when the dishwasher is open. To add insult to injury, the controls include a timer. What use this is when the controls are covered when in use is beyond me. If you peer through the crack, you can try to spot the numbers, but it's not very helpful as you're half guessing. The interior design is bad too. Every dishwasher is different, but I've never used another with such a bad layout on the racks. We can fit far fewer dishes into a load than we could with our previous dishwashers despite it being the same dimensions. The cycles take more than twice as long as well, which is lots of fun given how often we need to do two cycles a day now because of the poor layout. There are even more problems. The hose is set up very poorly and it won't go back into the body of the dishwasher unless it's still warm from having just finished the cycle. Sentence (English): Just know that Bosch doesn't use electric heating elements in this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Will not dry adequately dry dishes ] || ---------------- || Just know that Bosch doesn't use electric heating elements in this dishwasher. It relies on passive drying design. The design they use won't dry your dishes anywhere near as fast or as dry as a dishwasher with a heating element. Dishes always required towel wiping to get the last bit of water off them. Also, the rotary sprayer that attaches to the upper rack contains quite a bit of left over water. When you move the upper rack, the sprayer will release residual water onto whatever you have in the lower rack. The water doesn't look particular clean, either.We worked with Bosch customer support to make sure we were following recommended steps for optimal drying but it still required baby sitting the dishwashing cycle and didn't really help. Here's what they had us do to make no avail:- set water temp to 127 degrees- use a rinse aid- not put plastic or similar in the load- set the cycle to extra dry- open the dishwasher door as soon as the cycle completes to air dry. We're planning to dump this dishwasher and get one with a dryer heating element.

Sentence (English): While having owned the product for only a month, we are duly impressed with this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ What an upgrade from our elderly GE! ] || ---------------- || While having owned the product for only a month, we are duly impressed with this dishwasher. The construction, fit and finish, and overall quality is very good. The user's manual took a bit to get used to as it is written and arranged somewhat awkwardly (and maybe that's just our perception). It has done an excellent job cleaning the dishes et al. What a great improvement over our previous, 25 year old appliance! And quieter too. The controls are straight forward and you do *not* have to "hook-up" with the wifi/app if you don't want to (Editorial comment: It's a dishwasher, we can press buttons and close the door. You're already standing directly in front of it after loading it up, right? ). But if you want to program specific cycle set-ups, set start times, etc., go nuts; lots of features! Love the red dot light projected on the floor to indicate an active wash cycle and the tinkly chime when the load is done. If you are tall (and we are), you will have to bend down pretty significantly to open door fully to load the lower rack and close door again; door is hinged closer to the floor than our old dishwasher so we are getting used to that. The Bosch-Home website has many helpful videos. At this stage, we can certainly recommend this model if it's in your price point budget.

Sentence (English): Just know that Bosch doesn't use electric heating elements in this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Does not adequately dry dishes ] || ---------------- || Just know that Bosch doesn't use electric heating elements in this dishwasher. It relies on passive drying design. The design they use won't dry your dishes anywhere near as fast or as dry as a dishwasher with a heating element. Dishes always required towel wiping to get the last bit of water off them. Also, the rotary sprayer that attaches to the upper rack contains quite a bit of leftover water. When you move the upper rack, the sprayer will release residual water onto whatever you have in the lower rack. The water doesn't look particular clean, either. We worked with Bosch customer support to make sure we were following recommended steps for optimal drying but it still required babysitting the dishwashing cycle and didn't really help. Here's what they had us do to make no avail: - set water temp to 127 degrees - use a rinse aid - not put plastic or similar in the load - set the cycle to extra dry - open the dishwasher door as soon as the cycle completes to air dry. We're planning to dump this dishwasher and get one with a dryer heating element.

Sentence (English): I never thought I'd use the word "love" with a dishwasher, but indeed, after almost a month, that's how I feel.
Comments (English): [ Love on many levels—who would have known? ] || ---------------- || I never thought I'd use the word "love" with a dishwasher, but indeed, after almost a month, that's how I feel. I've suffered over the decades with Miele, Bosch, and Asko: loading them, especially deep soup bowls and dishes, was always frustrating, and so often the top rack filled up long before the bottom. Repairs on them also carry a foreign-appliance surcharge. I'm so glad I decided to follow friends' leads and make the switch to the USA-made KitchenAid. Comments (English): [ Love on many levels—who would have known? ] || ---------------- || I never thought I'd use the word \"love\" with a dishwasher, but indeed, after almost a month, that's how I feel. I've suffered over the decades with Miele, Bosch, and Asko: loading them, especially deep soup bowls and dishes, was always frustrating, and so often the top rack filled up long before the bottom. Repairs on them also carry a foreign-appliance surcharge. I'm so glad I decided to follow friends' leads and make the switch to the USA-made KitchenAid. The design of all three KitchenAid racks lets me load an astonishing amount very efficiently. I thought the interior lights might be a needless extravagance, but now I do appreciate them. I don't know whether it's the dishwasher itself (the dirt detection and spray systems) or the switch to the Finish Powerball quantum pods it came with that's made a difference, but dingy white bowls are now back to gleaming white.

Sentence (English): This is the third Bosch Dishwasher I have purchased in 15 years.
Comments (English): [ Bosch Benchmark ] || ---------------- || This is the third Bosch Dishwasher I have purchased in 15 years. The current Benchmark is better than the 2018 version in the following ways: 1) It has a better top of door button display that doesn't water spot like the previous "plexiglass" version. 2). The door feels more substantial when opening the door (less twisting/flex). 3) The time remaining light shining on the floor is nicer than the previous red dot. It falls short in the following areas: 1). There is NO delay function on the control panel. The delay is embedded in the app on your phone. I love tech but this is stupid. Also your App is terrible. From app: "Use My Schedule to easily specify a daily time in which you prefer your dishwasher to start – e.g. when the energy is greener, the rate is lower, or when you are sleeping. Instead of setting the delay start manually every time, you can define a preferred schedule. Your dishwasher automatically delays the washing to your desired time. Be aware that the dishwasher will not start on its own. Please press “Start” in the app after selecting the cycle." Pressing start in the app after loading the dishwasher is not convenient. 2). Zone control cleaning seems like a gimmick. 3). The top rolling rack is now designed for silverware/flatware and they took away one of the lower flatware rack/bins. 4). The top small rack rolls harder than previous 2018 model. 5). Crystal dry generally works good but it has some days where for some reason it doesn't work as well.

Sentence (English): We had our new Whirlpool dishwasher delivered a year and 4 months ago and at first we loved it.
Comments (English): [ Died After a Year ] || ---------------- || We had our new Whirlpool dishwasher delivered a year and 4 months ago and at first we loved it. The 3rd rack is very convenient, it was super quiet and it was great at cleaning the dishes. I didn't like how it did not dry the dishes very well, especially on the top rack, but I could deal with that. However, it suddenly stopped working last month and was flashing 2 codes. We liked it so we were hoping to get it repaired. After waiting a month for someone to come out and look at it, we were informed that the repairs would cost about as much as we paid for the dishwasher since it is outside the 1 year warranty. So now in addition to paying the $155 diagnostic fee, we need to either replace it entirely or pay for the parts plus an additional $150/hr in labor to get it fixed. I always thought Whirlpool was a good brand but this is not acceptable. An $800 dishwasher should last more than a little over a year. The control panel cover actually lifted up and that allowed steam to get under it and fried the panel. The repairmen said the seal on the dishwasher was okay so I am not sure how this happened ( and no, we did not open the door to allow steam to escape. ) We were told that the drain pump also needs replaced and that it is a common thing with these dishwashers for the pump to go bad. It looks like I better start looking for another brand of dishwasher to buy. If you decide to buy this dishwasher, you had better get the extended warranty or you may end up in the same situation.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher replaces a W brand that was about 11 years old and starting to show enough wear and tear.
Comments (English): [ Solid, Quiet Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher replaces a W brand that was about 11 years old and starting to show enough wear and tear. It is indeed quiet like others have mentioned (most noise is when draining water into the sink, but that is not the fault of the dishwasher). The dishes are coming out clean, too. I haven't decided yet if the silverware drawer is a blessing or a curse, because it means taller glasses cannot fit in the middle drawer. I may remove it and use the included basket instead-- not quite sure. The only other issue I have is that there seems to be no visual indicator of when the dishes are done. Sure, the red, running light is no longer on, but if you tend to start and forget, like leave for hours, you may not remember if it ran or if someone else emptied and reloaded. The old one had a green light to indicate clean. Maybe it is a setup issue I am missing. It sends a notification to my phone, too, but that only lets me know it is done once, not if someone else emptied and reloaded with dirty dishes. Other than the notifications and change in how I stack/load the dishes/glasses, it seems to be working extremely well. No more melted plastics (likely an issue of the other dishwasher going bad).

Sentence (English): This product and customer service has been the worst experience ever.
Comments (English): [ defective design, property damage, horrible servic ] || ---------------- || This product and customer service has been the worst experience ever. I have purchased this Smart Linear Wash 39dBA Dishwasher in Stainless Steel on 2023-08-29. There has been water leak due to a faulty design of the front panel which has caused a property damage to the kitchen floor and the base of the cabinets. The first water leak occurred on 2024-02-20 and the second water leak occurred on 2024-03-16. I engaged with Samsung support team via Samsung Care+ who have ended up sending 3 technicians through out the course of 3 months. 1st technician has falsely concluded that, although my video footage clearly captures water leaking out from the front panel, there is no water leak and it must be due to my fault for not cleaning the filter when I had only owned the dishwasher for 5 months. 2nd technician came out some weeks later and concluded that although he judges that the water leak is apparent, I have to take additional videos and call the Samsung support again because he cannot reproduce it on-site. Some weeks later, 3rd technician came out and installed an "aftermarket" repair kit specifically designed to fix this particular leaking issue. The repair worked for 1 week and the water started leaking again and eventually Samsung has issued a full refund on 2024-05-24. During this 9 months of ownership, there has been 6 occurrences of water leak which resulted in property damage, broken dishwasher, countless phone calls, and time wasted with the dishwasher and customer support. Samsung created a additional claim to provide compensation for the property damage. I was in contact with Specialty Claim manager initially to whom I provided all the details, evidence photos, videos and receipts and two repair estimates from professional contractors. Last time the Specialty Claim manager has communicated with me via email she said she will verify the 3 service history from the Samsung technicians back on 2024-08-20 and has never got back to me nor answered to my follow up emails and phone calls for 2 months. I am now trying to engage back with the Specialty Claim team to get an update but it is near impossible. I have called the Case manager directly but her phone number is not even reachable. So I am calling every 48 hours via the Samsung support number who claims that they are escalating this issue and that I will be getting a call from the Case Manager within 48 hours which never happens. I would advise people to stay clear from this product and the company to avoid potential property damage, lots of time wasted in trying to communicate with the customer support team, and all the stress it comes from it.

Media dishwasher uses a residual heat drying method, so even after washing dishes, more than 50% of the moisture remains, so I close the door for more than 30 minutes to dry them with the remaining residual heat, and then open the door slightly. If I wash the dishes in the evening, they don't dry well to the point that I have to clean them up around 12 noon the next day. Reason 2: It's cheap. The top and sides are stainless steel, but the bottom is made of plastic, so it dries slowly and there are a lot of water droplets on the floor. Reason 3: It doesn't have a sterilizing function. Reason 4: It's cheap. The tray angle doesn't lie flat, which is inconvenient. Large dishes such as pots and frying pans are bulky, but the tray itself doesn't lie flat, so the space is cramped. It's for 6 people, but in reality, rice bowls, soup bowls, plates. After putting in a few cups, there isn't enough space, so I thought it wouldn't be enough for two people to wash dishes, but in fact, when you boil soup, a pot comes out, a rice cooker comes out, and so on. So, you have to wash half of the dishes yourself or divide them into two, but it doesn't dry right away, and there is no separate function for drying, so it's impossible to use it twice in a row. *Summary (Advantages) It's good that the basket dishes such as fish and pork belly can be washed at high temperature. There were times when the dishes didn't wash well, but if you use powder detergent, they are cleaned neatly. At first, the dishes didn't wash well, so I washed them twice, and it turned out to be because of the detergent. There were times when the dishes didn't wash well because they didn't dissolve well, so I tried various detergents to see if it was a problem with the dishwasher or the detergent. I tried three types in total: 1 tablet, liquid, and powder. When I put in 1 tablet, it was a detergent + enzyme + rinse agent. The rinse agent didn't work, so I bought the liquid version again and used it. The liquid was better than putting in 1 tablet, but there were many times when it didn't work properly. Then, a neighbor gave me just Powdered detergent is really good, so I'm currently using the powder one. I heard there's a liquid one that you can use by tearing the plastic, but I'm going to try that next time. Also, if you don't use rinse aid, water droplets will form on the dishes, so it's better to use it. It was good value for money as a beginner's dishwasher, but if I were to buy it again next time, I'd choose the 12-person one and use one with a stainless steel bottom. Choose one with separate sterilization and drying functions. And I heard that there are ones that only wash a small amount of dishes at the top. Even though I don't have a lot of dishes, the dishwasher is seriously terrible. I tried to use it without complaining because it's cheap, but I usually wash the dishes twice or wash them myself. I'll use it more and revise the rating after using it more to see if it was my fault or the detergent. I once spun it on one frying pan that didn't get cleaned, and it didn't get cleaned at all, even though it wasn't hard. Detergent choice and the direction and position of the dishes are important, but ultimately, I think some dishwashers don't clean well. At first, the dishes didn't wash well, so I washed them in two batches. It turned out to be the detergent. Sometimes the dishes didn't wash well because they weren't dissolved well, so I tried various detergents to see if it was the dishwasher or the detergent. I tried three types in total: single-tablet, liquid, and powder. Single-tablet detergent combined detergent + enzyme + rinse. The rinse aid didn't work. I bought the liquid version again, but the liquid was better than single-tablet, but it often didn't work properly. However, a neighbor gave me a really good powder detergent, so I'm using the powder version now. I heard there's a liquid version that you tear open a plastic bag to use. I'm going to try that next time. And if you don't use rinse aid, water droplets will form on the dishes, so it's better to use it. That's because if I put in a few dishes, it's full, so I wash half the dishes myself and then half again. The dishes still stained, so I even switched to liquid detergent. I tried to use it without complaining because it's cheap, but I usually end up washing it twice, or even having to wash it myself. I'll revise my rating after using it more and seeing if it was my mistake or the detergent's fault. I even ran one frying pan that didn't get cleaned, and it didn't get cleaned at all. It wasn't that hard. So. Detergent selection is important, and the direction and position of the dishes are important, but in conclusion, I think there are dishwashers that don't clean well. It's supposed to serve six, but after adding rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, and a few cups, the space is tight. I thought it wouldn't be enough for two people to do the dishes, but when you boil soup, you have to use the pot and rice cooker, and so on. So I end up doing half the dishes myself. I need to do it in two batches, but since it doesn't dry immediately and doesn't have a separate drying function, it's actually impossible to use it twice in a row. *Summary (Pros) . It's great for basket dishes like fish and pork belly because it can be washed at high temperatures. Sometimes the dishes don't wash well, but powder detergent makes them clean. At first, the dishes didn't wash well, so I washed them in two batches. It turned out to be the detergent. Sometimes the dishes didn't wash well because they weren't dissolved well, so I tried various detergents to see if it was the dishwasher or the detergent. I tried three types in total: single-tablet, liquid, and powder. Single-tablet detergent combined detergent + enzyme + rinse. The rinse aid didn't work. I bought the liquid version again, but the liquid was better than single-tablet, but it often didn't work properly. However, a neighbor gave me a really good powder detergent, so I'm using the powder version now. I heard there's a liquid version that you tear open a plastic bag to use. I'm going to try that next time. And if you don't use rinse aid, water droplets will form on the dishes, so it's better to use it. It was a good value for the price as a starter, but if I were to buy again, I'd choose the 12-person model with a stainless steel bottom. Choose one with separate sterilization and drying functions. Some even wash small amounts of dishes at the top. This was my first dishwasher, so I didn't know much, so I'm leaving a rambling review in case it helps! November 8, 2011 One-month review. I'm leaving an additional review because the dishwasher doesn't wash well! I usually run it for 59 minutes at the P2 standard. That's because if I put in a few dishes, it's full, so I wash half the dishes myself and then half again. The dishes still stained, so I even switched to liquid detergent. It was so bad that I thought there was a problem with the product. I even had a neighbor who can't live without a dishwasher teach me how to properly place the dishes. Even though I don't have a lot of dishes, the dishwasher just doesn't wash well. I tried to use it without complaining because it's cheap, but I usually end up washing it twice, or even having to wash it myself. I'll revise my rating after using it more and seeing if it was my mistake or the detergent's fault. I even ran one frying pan that didn't get cleaned, and it didn't get cleaned at all. It wasn't that hard. So. Detergent selection is important, and the direction and position of the dishes are important, but in conclusion, I think there are dishwashers that don't clean well. It falls short in the following areas:. 1). There is NO delay function on the control panel. The delay is embedded in the app on your phone. I love tech but this is stupid. Also your App is terrible. From app: "Use My Schedule to easily specify a daily time in which you prefer your dishwasher to start – e.g. when the energy is greener, the rate is lower, or when you are sleeping. Be aware that the dishwasher will not start on its own. Please press “Start” in the app after selecting the cycle.". Pressing start in the app after loading the dishwasher is not convenient. 2). Zone control cleaning seems like a gimmick. 3). The top rolling rack is now designed for silverware/flatware and they took away one of the lower flatware rack/bins. 4). The top small rack rolls harder than previous 2018 model. 5). Crystal dry generally works good but it has some days where for some reason it doesn't work as well.

Sentence (English): Hit this to replace our old Bosch 500.
Comments (English): [ Works fine but some features require WiFi and app ] || ---------------- || Hit this to replace our old Bosch 500. Works well to wash, similar to the old one. The main frustration is that while it claims to have delayed start as a feature, that feature is only available by using the app. The old one had an easy to use button so it was easy to delay the start. This one requires setting up a special cycle or schedule on the app and can only be delayed by starting through the app. This is sort of a pain if the phone isn't around when done loading. Sometimes I have to go upstairs to start the delay start through the app. Som I suppose this model technically has a delayed start feature, but it's on the verge of false advertising to claim that is a feature without mentioning that it is only available through the app. I'd give it 5 stars just for cleaning but the misrepresentation about feature is frustrating, and we feel like this is a downgrade from our prior Bosch 500 in terms of ease of use.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher gets the dishes clean, which is the important part.
Comments (English): [ cleans nice ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher gets the dishes clean, which is the important part. There were several new and strange things I had to learn about this dishwasher. First, I could put plastics in the bottom rack. With no heating element it doesn't matter where the plastic or flatware or anything is put, it still gets clean. Second, It was strange not rinsing the dishes before washing, only removing the food. I have never had a dishwasher with the 'auto' feature that senses how dirty the dishes are. Third, it took several days running the dishwasher for the dishes to start drying. Now each load is pretty dry but the walls of the dishwasher are still very wet. I prop the dishwasher open a bit to allow the insides to dry, similar to what I do with the washing machine. Next, It is hard to get used to putting the flatware in the top rack like the video shows, I am so used to using a basket made for the flatware. Finally, the bottom rack does not have a stop. Each time I slide the bottom rack out it rolls off of the rail onto the open door and I have to pick it up and position it back on the rail inside the dishwasher. All in all I am happy with the dishwasher, the things I wish would be different are the bottom rack not having a stop and the walls of the dishwasher walls still wet even though the dishes are dry.

Sentence (English): This was advertised as a tall tub dishwasher; it is not.
Comments (English): [ Door Open Dry has a design flaw. It's not ready. ] || ---------------- || This was advertised as a tall tub dishwasher; it is not. It is ADA compliant, which means it is a shorter tub and, when installed into a standard opening, about 3 inches of space are lost underneath as nylon screw pads are intended to hoist the unit up on stilts until it is high enough to fit. However, two of the screw feet were missing from the empty slots. I had to order those parts which took several extra days to ship. The door open dry feature (which kicks the door open at the end of a cycle to allow dishes to air dry) does not work because the door spring is not designed for such a feature. To kick the door open, a push bar extends and quickly retracts - and the springs on the door hinge simply close the door again. There is no partially open detent position for the door to remain in; it does not exist in this design. It appears like the feature was hastily implemented and put to market without it actually working. If you take the side panel off and examine the spring system, you can see there is no aftermarket fix or repair for this. Others have noted the awkward upper tray design which makes placing items tricky. Be careful. This is a special/delivered order appliance item. This item is non-returnable at my big box store. If it is delivered to your home, once you sign for it, it's yours for keeps.

Sentence (English): Seems like a great machine, but the user interfaces are confusing, and it's too reliant on the app.
Comments (English): [ Well engineered, poorly designed ] || ---------------- || Seems like a great machine, but the user interfaces are confusing, and it's too reliant on the app. For example, on older machines by other companies I can hit "+4 hour delay" just to get a delay. With this one I have to hit a delay button that increments initially by MINUTES. Why? WHo wants to delay their cycle by a few minutes? And don't even get me started on the app. No one needs an app, but it's the only way to set a "favorite" which I assumed would include the setting to start via a delay (or the confusing My Schedule). But the favorite, when saved to the dishwasher, DOES NOT INCLUDE TIMING. It just starts immediately. You can only leverage My Schedule with the app. Also the rack layouts feel really frustrating and inefficient. Huge gaps in the bottom rack mean that even medium sized things need the be on the tines or placed carefully. The upper rack has weird angles and seems to be missing a row of tines down the center. The thing cleans well and dries decently, though it isn't as silent as the reviews seemed to indicate. It makes a lot of noise when pumping water. I'm hoping that it holds up well, which might make it worth the annoyances and cost. But it seems like such a shame to have a well engineered appliance with an overcomplicated, over-digitized interface. Just give us the buttons. App reliance is not high end or luxury. Luxury is simplicity and good design.

Sentence (English): If you self install, you find the KitchenAid Model Model KDTM404KPS Dishwasher has cheaped out on some things.
Comments (English): [ Cheaped Out 0n Some Things, but Still Good ] || ---------------- || If you self install, you find the KitchenAid Model Model KDTM404KPS Dishwasher has cheaped out on some things. The insulation blanket is not affixed to the unit and just lays over the top and down the sides. It does not cover the corners of the stainless tub. Because you have to adjust the back legs prior to sliding the DW into the opening, the insulation blanket will move and bunch up because there is nothing holding it in place. I had to tape the bottom back corner sections together so when sliding into the opening it keeps the blanket from being pushed out. The use of a plastic garden hose connector for the hot water plumbing is just cheap. What happened to the brass? Oh, cost cutting. I have read where some complain about leaks because of this type of connector. Because this DW does not come with the 90 degree hose connector you have to buy it, or buy their expensive kit. The leaking complaints have to do with improper threads. Make sure the connector has the correct "Hose" threads.Also this DW is designed to connect the electrical prior to installing. Newer homes will have a AC receptacle in the cabinet next to the DW and you connect the electrical cord and plug before install. Most homes still have a direct AC wire in the DW opening. If you have direct wire then you have to connect after the DW is in place in the opening. Because the opening for the wire in the DW terminal box is at the back wall of the terminal, it is very difficult to properly install the wire because of very little access. With the DW partially in so oyu have side access, you will have to measure the length of the wire end to install the "Strain Relief" first as there is no way to tighten the strain relief screws after inserting the wire into the terminal box.As for the the operation of the dishwasher, I found it very good. It is more quiet than my high dollar Samsung that only lasted 8 years. Everything works as designed. I wash my dishes at night while watching TV and open the DW door slightly when finished. In the morning I unload the DW and everything is dry. I do not use the heated dry option as it is not needed in this scenario. For those who need dishes right after washing, I can see where the dishes can still be somewhat wet. If needed get the DW with fan dry option. There are complaints about the basket design/layout. After 8 years with my other DW you get use to its layout and I too have some complaints, but nothing insurmountable. Give it time and you will adapt. Then when you get your next DW, not of the same brand, you'll complain again because it is not like this one.Overall, I am satisfied with this DW and do recommend it if you can get it on a good sale. Now I have only had it for a week. There are no leaks, it is quiet, it looks good, the controls all work, and everything works as designed. Only time will tell how well it is built. The days of appliances lasting 20 years or more are gone. Most repairmen I have had out over the years, tell me major appliances are now designed to last only 7 to 10 years. The more bells and whistles, the more to go wrong.

Sentence (English): If you self install, you find the KitchenAid Model Model KDTM404KPS Dishwasher has cheaped out on some things.
Comments (English): [ Cheaped Out 0n Some Things, but Still Good ] || ---------------- || If you self install, you find the KitchenAid Model Model KDTM404KPS Dishwasher has cheaped out on some things. The insulation blanket is not affixed to the unit and just lays over the top and down the sides. It does not cover the corners of the stainless tub. Because you have to adjust the back legs prior to sliding the DW into the opening, the insulation blanket will move and bunch up because there is nothing holding it in place. I had to tape the bottom back corner sections together so when sliding into the opening it keeps the blanket from being pushed out. The use of a plastic garden hose connector for the hot water plumbing is just cheap. What happened to the brass? Oh, cost cutting. I have read where some complain about leaks because of this type of connector. Because this DW does not come with the 90 degree hose connector you have to buy it, or buy their expensive kit. The leaking complaints have to do with improper threads. Make sure the connector has the correct \"Hose\" threads. Also this DW is designed to connect the electrical prior to installing. Newer homes will have a AC receptacle in the cabinet next to the DW and you connect the electrical cord and plug before install. Most homes still have a direct AC wire in the DW opening. If you have direct wire then you have to connect after the DW is in place in the opening. Because the opening for the wire in the DW terminal box is at the back wall of the terminal, it is very difficult to properly install the wire because of very little access. With the DW partially in so oyu have side access, you will have to measure the length of the wire end to install the \"Strain Relief\" first as there is no way to tighten the strain relief screws after inserting the wire into the terminal box. As for the the operation of the dishwasher, I found it very good. It is more quiet than my high dollar Samsung that only lasted 8 years. Everything works as designed. I wash my dishes at night while watching TV and open the DW door slightly when finished. In the morning I unload the DW and everything is dry. I do not use the heated dry option as it is not needed in this scenario. For those who need dishes right after washing, I can see where the dishes can still be somewhat wet. If needed get the DW with fan dry option. There are complaints about the basket design/layout. After 8 years with my other DW you get use to its layout and I too have some complaints, but nothing insurmountable. Give it time and you will adapt. Then when you get your next DW, not of the same brand, you'll complain again because it is not like this one. Overall, I am satisfied with this DW and do recommend it if you can get it on a good sale. Now I have only had it for a week. There are no leaks, it is quiet, it looks good, the controls all work, and everything works as designed. Only time will tell how well it is built. The days of appliances lasting 20 years or more are gone. Most repairmen I have had out over the years, tell me major appliances are now designed to last only 7 to 10 years. The more bells and whistles, the more to go wrong.

Sentence (English): We replaced a Samsung with a failed pump with the Bosch dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Happy with it ] || ---------------- || We replaced a Samsung with a failed pump with the Bosch dishwasher. So far, we've been very happy with the Bosch. It is VERY quiet, cleans better than the Samsung, and seems well engineered. Most of the time, the only way you can tell it's running is by the running light it shines on the floor. I also like that the upper rack has three possible positions versus two for other dishwashers. There are some learning curves though - especially on how to load the dishwasher. We used to use the silverware basket on the Samsung, but the top silverware rack on the Bosch works better for us (I took out the Bosch basket for more room on the first rack). Also, I mostly leave the foldable tines on the lower rack in the down position so I can load pots and pans. As other reviewers have said, the tines on those are too close together to really be useful. I did the installation myself and it was fairly easy. The major task was adding an outlet for the cord (the Samsung was hardwired), but the rest of the install was pretty simple.

Comments (English): [ Call it 4.5 stars ] || ---------------- || The good news: This dishwasher is *really* quiet. Slightly less good: The 3-level racks take some getting used to, and the top rack is quite limited in terms of space and arrangement. Also, some items require a little towel-drying after the standard drying cycle — but we accept that as better than the cost (in time and energy) of the Extra Dry setting. On the whole, a good selection, and Home Depot's installation was on time and well done.

I didn't know until I read the complete manual and watched several YouTube videos about this problem that I figured it out. Now I don't have any problems with leaking. The heat from the dry cycle will seal the gasket to the door of the dishwasher.

Sentence (English): Never have had so many issues with an appliance.
Comments (English): [ Hasn't been fun ] || ---------------- || Never have had so many issues with an appliance. Within the first year I started having the unit Turn off/on randomly. Wasn't a problem unless I needed to use it and it was off. Sometimes I had to simply flip the breaker. Sometimes I had to unplug the unit for a few hours then plug back in. Sometimes I'd have to disconnect the electrical connections underneath the unit and reconnect them. Sometimes I'd have to open the junction box underneath the unit and disconnect the power cord, then wire nut the connections back together. Sometimes I'd have to pull the lower rack out and vacuum suck any existing water in the drain (if there was any), then unplug the unit and let it set for a couple hours then plug it back in to power on. I've been doing this for about 3 1/2 years of ownership and finally I think the control board has given out completely which has obviously been the problem since I pretty much bought this unit. Now I get to buy a replacement for around $200 on a unit I've been troubleshooting/servicing almost weekly for roughly 3 1/2 yrs just to keep it functioning this long. This has not been a good experience at all and that's stating it mildly. That's my honest experience and review of this Dishwasher unfortunately.

Also, she told me that I needed to make sure all my dishes were facing the same direction. Neither of these is something I've had to do with cheaper models of dishwashers. I tried her recommendations, and my dishes are still sporadically being cleaned. It makes me wonder if I've been eating off dirty dishes for 4 months now. Sentence (English): Why are the racks so chintzy on an $1100 dishwasher?
Comments (English): [ Seems like Junk ] || ---------------- || Why are the racks so chintzy on an $1100 dishwasher? The build quality of this thing is horrendous. The tines on the racks are so thin, I can't imagine them lasting more than a few years. The whole upper and lower racks flex under normal use. It really does seem extremely cheap.The latch system has no adjustment to tighten the door seal. The door literally flexes 1/4 inch from left to right like it's made out of the thinnest metal possible. The dishwasher is leaking steam / condensation and creating drips on the counter-top above it. GE's solution, no seriously, there is a service bulletin about this. Their solution is to have a technician apply a bead of silicone INSIDE the dishwasher (on the stainless steel surface that is supposed to be sanitary) on the seam of the tub. So that's a 28 inch bead of silicone from top left to top right (you can feel the seam just on the inside of the door seal if you run your finger along the top of the inside of the dishwasher). This is supposed to fix the problem. I laughed and rejected that as a viable repair. I feel sorry for anyone with the same problem who let a technician do this. That's just insane! $1100 dishwasher, GE says, "oh we'll just slap some silicone all around the inside of it to try to seal it up better" Heh. talk about ridiculous. $1100 "Cafe" dishwasher still has 4 manual level legs including 2 in the back which are impossible to adjust unless you pull the dishwasher back out, instead of having a front leveling system.It looks like the latch design traverses all of GE's dishwashers so maybe I got a bad apple, but this build quality of this thing reminds me of a $400 dishwasher. That being said, the dishwasher does clean well, but man, I guess I just expected more and am very disappointed. I have a case with GE, don't give up as they will likely be replacing this dishwasher although I don't really have any confidence that rack quality would improve even up to the Monogram series, which I may go take a look at in person just to see. Absolutely poor poor fit and finish and durability on this thing. For all the raving reviews, take a closer look!

Comments (English): [ A cost-effective objet d's table with all the necessary functions ] || ---------------- || Reason for Purchase: We currently use an Objet DEBJ4ES dishwasher (22 model, now discontinued) at home. I originally recommended a model with a hot air drying function, just like ours, but my mom said she didn't really need it. So, I looked for a cost-effective option and ended up purchasing this model! Product Features: Although Objet dishwashers all look quite similar in design, the prices vary widely depending on the internal structure and performance. Based on my comparison, the key features of this DUE1BGL model are as follows: 12-place setting, 2-tier internal structure: In 3-tier structures, the top compartment is for holding cutlery, but my mom looked at it and said she would prefer a cutlery holder rather than having to put items in one by one. This product has a cutlery holder, so you can simply load items upright. Control buttons are located on the front: Depending on the Objet design, the control buttons may be on the top or the front; this product has them on the front. Hot Air Drying X, High Temperature Drying O, Automatic Door Opening O. : Since our dishwasher currently uses hot air drying, I was worried whether everything would dry properly if I only used high temperature drying. Yesterday, my mom loaded it with dishes and ran it for 1 hour plus high temperature drying, and she said that everything was completely dry with no moisture left, except for one ceramic cup. Features found in high-end products (interior lighting, glide rails, knife/scissor holder/frying pan shelf) are missing. : While some of these features are nice to have, I don't think they are strictly necessary. Yesterday, as a test, she put in an old square plate full of grease and ran it through the machine; she was satisfied that it was cleaned thoroughly. This product seems to have exactly the necessary features among the Objet dishwashers! I recommend it as a cost-effective product. -------------------------------------------------------------------------. If you found my post helpful, I would appreciate it if you clicked "Helpful"! Sentence (English): This has not been a good experience.
Comments (English): [ A disappointing experience. ] || ---------------- || This has not been a good experience. We purchased this product as an open box item in \"excellent\" condition which Best Buy confirms \"look(s) brand new — with no physical flaws, scratches or scuffs\". I drove 60 miles (120 total) to collect it at their Brockton, MA store and was assured by the sales assistant that it was as described. It was heavily wrapped in plastic so I took their word. My mistake. When I got home it had several very obvious dents on the front door. Best Buy customer service was unable to reclassify it as being in fair condition and credit me the difference. Instead, she set up a scheduled phone call (you can't call them directly) for me to speak directly with the store. They never called me back. And I couldn't take another 3 hours to return it. So I went ahead and plumbed it in - which brings me to part 2 of this review - the product has multiple design failings:. 1) The lower rack has to be physically lifted up to make it over the interior rack rail onto the front door rail - they are not aligned. Or you can pull the rack out, have it hit the door rail and risk displacing all your items. 2) The lower rack tines which separate the dishes can theoretically be set to one of several angles by adjusting their position and engaging them in a ratchet. Unfortunately, the materials are made of such cheap plastic that they don't stay in place and flip-flop with the slightest touch. Terrible. 3) The space below the tines described in 2 above is so large (and lacking any cross beam) that objects that are not round in shape and with a diameter of a large plate, stick through or fall through the gap to the bottom of the dishwasher. 4) Do not buy this unit if you plan to have it to the left of your sink. The shape and angle of the tines and the position of the silverware basket is designed for practical use only if the dishwasher is to the left of your sink and only if you're left-handed. Amazing. 5) Finally, there's some crazy air circulator feature that keeps going on and humming any time of day and night - even with the door open. 6) Several of my items don't come out clean - even after setting to heavy load. In summary, a junk dishwasher for the price and buyer beware. Also, an extremely disappointing experience with Best Buy's customer service. Beware of their open box items.

Comments (English): [ Don't EVER buy appliances from samsung.com ] || ---------------- || I have been waiting for my dishwasher to be installed over 1 month, and it still HAS NOT been installed. The box is left unopened, and Samsung.com says that I cannot return it because it passed the returning period."What? It was not even installed, and it is left on the floor as unopened"Let me tell you how Samsung.com works and why I do NOT recommend buying products at Samsung.comThe problem is that they are working with a chain of outsourced companies.: samsung.com -> RXO at GA -> RXO at each state -> local appliance agents -> local handyman/installer.Samsung doesn't really have much control on the RXO and the actual installers. I have been calling with all of them over a month, and each of the outsourced companies tells me different stories each time I give them a call. Each individual that I have spoken to seems friendly. But, again, this is a structural problem. They just hire too many outsourcing companies just to save costs.If I purchased the appliances from a local LOWE's, Home Depot, or Costco, this wouldn't happen. I can go to the shop where I purchased the appliances, and they can communicate with all the installers and delivery staffs directly. It's super beneficial that the sellers hire the installers directly. In contrast, samsung.com is running with layers and layers of outsourcing companies.- They outsource the delivery and installation to a company called, RXO.- RXO outsource the delivery and installation to a local RXO in each state.- The local RXO outsource the work to a local movers and workers.In my case, RXO doesn't really have much control on the local movers and installers. They left appliances on the floor one and half months ago, and the appliances are still NOT installed yet.I phoned to samsung.com and RXO tens of times, but what they all do is just passing the message to the next outsourcing companies. This is the problem where the seller doesn't hire the final labour/workers directly.The worst thing is that I cannot even return the items, although the appliances are just left as unopened on the floor. This would not be acceptable if this was purchased by a local appliance shop. They take care of the total care from purchase to installation. However, samsung.com is just for selling the products, and they just connect the appliances to other outsourcing companies for the rest. Whether the appliances are installed or not is NOT part of what they offer.In short, I highly recommend staying away from samsung.com. I am a fan of samsung.com products, and I still think they make good products. However, I will never buy anything from samsung.com.If you are considering to buy a samsung product at samsung.com, mainly due to their competitive prices, you should look for other places. You may think you don't need customer services. At least for appliances, there happens to be problems in installation and maintenance. Use LOWE's or Costco. It's worth paying extra dollar for the after-sales customer care. samsung.com basically does nothing other than passing messages to the outsourcing companies, once they sell products.

We have only had it for a month but I can't imagine going back to our other dishwasher.

Sentence (English): We previously had a Bosch dishwasher that lasted about 10 years, with a single repair due to not properly draining, but ultimately the same issue recurred.
Comments (English): [ Not as expected ] || ---------------- || We previously had a Bosch dishwasher that lasted about 10 years, with a single repair due to not properly draining, but ultimately the same issue recurred. We were generally happy with the prior model, so decided to buy Bosch again. We like quiet dishwashers that dry well. We were assured both would be the case for this one, especially the drying since it had the "Crystal Dry" on it. Well, the Crystal Dry isn't even as good as the prior model at drying dishes, as I have to open the door and leave it open for hours for the dishes to air dry. Secondly, they removed the delay option (assuming you'd hook it up to a smart phone, I'm sure, but our installer recommended against doing so due to issues he has seen with this option). Thirdly, the old dishwasher would provide a light that says whether the dishes are clean immediately following running a cycle, but this one doesn't tell you anything. Finally, the manual is close to worthless and there are two options on the dishwasher the manual says nothing about. Not sure I'd choose Bosch again after this experience.

Sentence (English): Purchased this to replace a 30 year old Maytag.
Comments (English): [ Fantastic Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Purchased this to replace a 30 year old Maytag. This dischwasher is quiet, well built, cleans exceptionally well, and the layout of the inside racks is very good. We really like the third level silverware rack. Gets silverware clean and is easy to load and unload. The adjustable features of the top rack and middle rack enable different sized items to fit well. My one complaint is on the bottom rack, while the back two rows can individually lay down, I would like it better if they were split in the middle so that you could create a flat area in 1/4 of the bottom tray. Or even better, if when you layed down those tines, a couple of wider spaced pot tines would become available. The features on this machine are excellent - from the crystal dry, to the half load, and extra scrubbing, everything gets very clean. Running it on Auto takes all the guesswork out of setting the machine and consistently gives us an excellent wash. I used to "pre-wash" my dishes to ensure they would get clean in my old machine. When I got the Bosch, I tested it by putting dishes and pots straight in from the table or the stove, with everything coming out spotless. This really saves me time and water when cleaning up. We are extremely happy with this purchase and look forward to many years of service.

The features on this machine are excellent - from the crystal dry, to the half load, and extra scrubbing, everything gets very clean.  Running it on Auto takes all the guesswork out of setting the machine and consistently gives us an excellent wash.  I used to 'pre-wash' my dishes to ensure they would get clean in my old machine.  When I got the Bosch, I tested it by putting dishes and pots straight in from the table or the stove, with everything coming out spotless.  This really saves me time and water when cleaning up. We are extremely happy with this purchase and look forward to many years of service.

Sentence (English): This has not been a good experience.
Comments (English): [ A disappointing experience. ] || ---------------- || This has not been a good experience. We purchased this product as an open box item in "excellent" condition which Best Buy confirms "look(s) brand new — with no physical flaws, scratches or scuffs". I drove 60 miles (120 total) to collect it at their Brockton, MA store and was assured by the sales assistant that it was as described. It was heavily wrapped in plastic so I took their word. My mistake. When I got home it had several very obvious dents on the front door. Best Buy customer service was unable to reclassify it as being in fair condition and credit me the difference. Instead, she set up a scheduled phone call (you can't call them directly) for me to speak directly with the store. They never called me back. And I couldn't take another 3 hours to return it. So I went ahead and plumbed it in - which brings me to part 2 of this review - the product has multiple design failings:1) The lower rack has to be physically lifted up to make it over the interior rack rail onto the front door rail - they are not aligned. Or you can pull the rack out, have it hit the door rail and risk displacing all your items.2) The lower rack tines which separate the dishes can theoretically be set to one of several angles by adjusting their position and engaging them in a ratchet. Unfortunately, the materials are made of such cheap plastic that they don't stay in place and flip-flop with the slightest touch. Terrible.3) The space below the tines described in 2 above is so large (and lacking any cross beam) that objects that are not round in shape and with a diameter of a large plate, stick through or fall through the gap to the bottom of the dishwasher.4) Do not buy this unit if you plan to have it to the left of your sink. The shape and angle of the tines and the position of the silverware basket is designed for practical use only if the dishwasher is to the left of your sink and only if you're left-handed. Amazing.5) Finally, there's some crazy air circulator feature that keeps going on and humming any time of day and night - even with the door open.6) Several of my items don't come out clean - even after setting to heavy load.In summary, a junk dishwasher for the price and buyer beware. Also, an extremely disappointing experience with Best Buy's customer service. Beware of their open box items.
